subject: general
question: How does a loop act as a contraceptive?

options.text: It blocks the release of sperm.
It inhibits implantation of the embryo.
It blocks access to the fallopian tubes.

solution:
The correct answer is __**It blocks access to the fallopian tubes**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• This is for informational purposes only. For medical advice or diagnosis, consult a professional.
 
• A loop, in the context of contraception, generally refers to an Intrauterine Device (IUD). IUDs are small, T-shaped devices inserted into the uterus by a healthcare provider to prevent pregnancy. 
 
• Here's how different types of IUDs work:
 
• **Copper IUDs:**
 
 
• These IUDs contain copper wire that creates a hostile environment for sperm. 
 
• Copper ions released by the IUD impair sperm motility and function, preventing them from reaching and fertilizing an egg. 
 
• They also trigger an inflammatory response in the uterus, making it less hospitable for sperm survival. 
 
• Hormonal IUDs:
 
• These IUDs release small amounts of progestin, a type of female hormone. 
 
• Progestin thickens the cervical mucus, making it difficult for sperm to pass through. 
 
• It also thins the lining of the uterus (endometrium), making it less receptive for a fertilized egg to implant.
 
• Some hormonal IUDs may also prevent ovulation. 
 
• Key Points:
 
• IUDs are highly effective forms of long-term contraception. 
 
• They are inserted by a healthcare professional and can remain in place for several years, depending on the type. 
 
• IUDs are reversible. Once removed, fertility typically returns quickly. 
 
• IUDs offer several advantages, including convenience, long-term effectiveness, and minimal disruption to daily life.
